card.name: Tahtib (Tahteeb)
card.era: ancient (Old Kingdom roots); festive form from the New Kingdom
card.tagline: Ancient Egyptian stick art that became a festive dance
card.profile: Tahtib (tahteeb) is an Egyptian stick art from Upper Egypt that blends martial art, fencing and dance. Per UNESCO, which inscribed it in 2016, it involves a brief, non-violent interchange between two men each wielding a long stick (asa) while folk music plays; no striking is allowed and complete control must be shown. Rooted in ancient Egypt - depicted on New Kingdom temple walls at Luxor and Saqqara - it survives as a festive game among Sa'idi communities, embodying values of respect, courage, chivalry and pride.
card.insight: Tahtib is one of the oldest documented Egyptian performance traditions and the source of the women's Saidi cane dance; it is Egypt's UNESCO-listed intangible heritage, inscribed in 2016 (UNESCO; Egypt Museum).
card.image_significance: The 4,000-year-old stick dance. A representative image shows a line or row formation, often with canes, swords or flowing veils — Upper Egypt, Egypt.
